ambiguities.statement: Approve And Build and runtime-capable v2 contracts coexist with an explicit no-runtime-launch boundary; disabled-state GUI behavior, resulting receipt, and later activation authority are unspecified.

Governance registration may refresh Spec Lock, shards, evidence, graph, and decisions after stability, while PRD and Goal maps describe those artifacts as explicit-seal-only; phase equivalence is unclear.

Goal Runtime owns runtime write authority while consuming a readiness-only ledger/Plan boundary that creates no WorkNodes or NodeSeeds; the permitted execution/materialization boundary is not explicit here.
Instant Grep runtime fields exist only if promoted, and clarification consumers may ask questions, but promotion authority, timeout/default behavior, and unavailable-user handling are unnamed.
Browser permission precedence is called deterministic without being enumerated, and no rule explains how signal_confidence values constrain actions, recovery, or user warnings.
The web command family is ready-now while provider taxonomy, selection, routing, and ordering remain blocked, leaving effective-provider behavior unresolved.
Contracts_V0 promotion depends on whether remote identity/health fields are canonized beyond storage/UI prose, but that threshold and adjudicator are not defined.
Worktree context may appear at several surfaces only when ambiguity or conflicted state matters; priority, consistency, stale-ID handling, and the testable meaning of matters are unspecified.

builder_discretion.statement: Testing owners must determine current official sources and safe installation behavior, but this index supplies no freshness or trust oracle.
Model/account/provider owners determine requested/effective resolution consumed by Goal Runtime; failover and unavailable-provider policy are deferred.
Instant Grep runtime fields are conditional on promotion, and chat/audit consumers may clarify ambiguity without gaining final authority.
Provider taxonomy, routing internals, provider settings layout, and global/per-operation ordering UX are explicitly blocked from ready-now slash-command invention.
UI Command and GitHub docs may deepen additively only while retiring claims that smaller command sets are complete; remote persisted/event fields may trigger Contracts reconciliation.
GUI worktree context may use workspace, header, Source Control strip, editor status, or breadcrumb placement, but repeated per-row/per-tab symbols are disallowed by default.

candidate_findings.statement: Invisible/internal goals combine durable scheduling, child creation, attachments, and write authority without explicit privilege inheritance, disclosure, cancellation, resource caps, or adversarial-input boundaries.

The browser authority map exposes capture, persistence, recovery, auth handoff, and allow/ask/deny permissions without explicit origin isolation, sensitive-data capture rules, permission revocation, or hostile-page containment.
The request_id-to-blocked_sequence compatibility gate precedes runtime mutation but lacks atomicity, idempotency, replay, expiry, revocation, and TOCTOU semantics for scoped actions.

Instant Grep requires no silent local fallback while remote-cache verification, dirty-layer recovery, freshness, cache authenticity, overload, and degraded/offline user behavior remain unexpressed in the index map.
Terminal packets are non-buildable without UI_Command_Catalog, Contracts_V0, and Wiring_Matrix, yet the section ContractRef omits all three required command/contract/wiring owners.
One-bounded-auto-retry remote reconnect, shared buffers, multi-root handoff, and command coherence lack failure atomicity, stale-state validation, and executable acceptance beyond document inclusion.

Debug packetization mandates Commands, Glossary, Wiring, Contracts, Prompt Pipeline, and GitHub coverage, but its ContractRef omits those mandatory companions and supplies no semantic or executable closure oracle.
Approve And Build and runtime-capable schemas have no specified truthful disabled-state behavior while the compile explicitly cannot launch runtime or emit artifacts.

claims.statement: PRD_Builder owns intake through Approved PRD Pack and explicit Wizard handoff; Planning_Wizard owns PlanningRun through ApprovedPlanPack and Approve And Build; strict runtime contracts exist, but runtime launch, artifacts, executable work, builds, and dispatch remain disabled.

Goal_Runtime owns invisible/internal goals, durable scheduler state, attachments, child goals, weak-model safety, write authority, approval boundaries, evidence, and completion; chat owns visible controls, while contract, storage, permission, model, provider, and artifact owners supply consumed state.

Instant Grep authority is split across Tools query/fallback semantics, storage dirty-layer publication/recovery, FinalGUI disclosure/settings, and GitHub remote-cache verification with no silent local fallback; consumers may clarify ambiguity but final decisions follow canonical owners.

Section15 owns browser behavior, sessions, actions, capture, permissions, persistence, recovery, and non-goals; rewrite-tie-in owns architecture; browser confidence values are closed to four enums, and stale runtime, permission, capture, and placement alternatives are retired.

Slash-command reconciliation is locked into four owner phases; ready-now scope includes web operations, permissions, provenance, bounded defaults, and payloads, while provider taxonomy, routing internals, settings layout, and provider-ordering UX remain blocked.

Artifact, HITL, and tool approval authority is split by presentation, persistence, envelope, policy, UX, and permission semantics; request_id must resolve to blocked_sequence before mutation, and new approvals use blocked_sequence, approval_scope_key, and ordered allowed_action_ids without scope widening.

Terminal behavior, placement, persistence, commands, events, wiring, policy, health, permissions, and terminology have separate owners; packets omitting UI_Command_Catalog, Contracts_V0, or Wiring_Matrix are declared non-buildable.

File/editor reconciliation locks Crosswalk, GitHub remote retry, LSP fallback, FileManager shared-buffer behavior, runtime identity/persistence, and FinalGUI placement ownership; packetization requires command wiring, stale-canon replacement, and a MUST CHANGE/RECONCILE/VERIFY register.

Remote/event identity can promote Contracts_V0 from verification to reconciliation; worktree lifecycle stays outside FileManager, repo_id/worktree_id must survive Source Control handoff, and GUI context appears when multi-root, non-default, ambiguous, or conflicted state matters.

Debug ownership spans chat lifecycle, runtime posture, persisted investigation state, browser automation/auth/takeover, artifacts/events/prompts/tools, GUI and remote consumers; two mandatory document triplets must remain in scope to avoid semantic, persistence, prompt, routing, and remote drift.

cross_window_seams.statement: Backward context establishes design-only PlanCompile, Executor/Goal ownership, receipt/evidence boundaries, and disabled runtime assumptions consumed by the PRD map.
The PRD map delegates lifecycle details to schema and owner documents outside this window, while retaining a strict no-launch boundary.
Goal Runtime depends on ledger, PlanUnit, readiness, provider, permission, storage, chat, GUI, and artifact owners not reviewed here.

Browser, terminal, file/editor, and debug maps repeatedly intersect Section15, FinalGUI, storage, commands, permissions, GitHub, artifacts, and wiring, creating cross-packet precedence and synchronized-reconciliation seams.
Forward context begins the broader authoritative Plan table and restates canonical roles for rewrite, Section15, chat, FinalGUI, GitHub, FileManager, LSP, storage, ledger, and Plan docs.
Legacy chain-wizard material remains lineage in both PRD/Goal maps and the forward owner table, while GitHub still references it for legacy examples.

invalid_reason: Substantive reviewer agent identities were reused across successive window/role assignments, violating the Fresh Agent Isolation Protocol.

negative_space_observations.statement: Testing research, safe installation, Auto/On/Off behavior, redaction, and receipts lack freshness periods, offline behavior, supply-chain verification, rollback, privilege limits, and failure defaults in this window.

Invisible goals, child goals, attachments, scheduler updates, weak-model safety, and write authority lack explicit recursion/resource limits, privilege inheritance, disclosure, cancel/kill, duplicate scheduling, crash recovery, and malicious-attachment handling.

Instant Grep lacks stated behavior for stale readers, concurrent publication, corrupt/dirty indexes, rebuild overload, false negatives, hostile regexes, poisoned remote caches, offline no-fallback operation, and analytics privacy.

Browser ownership mentions permissions, capture, persistence, and recovery without stating origin isolation, cookie/credential boundaries, downloads, clipboard, local files, certificate failures, permission revocation, capture redaction, or hostile-page containment.

Slash-command phases lack partial-apply rollback/resume, parser and alias-conflict handling, malicious payload/tool-output behavior, provenance spoofing defenses, and user-visible behavior when ready-now web operations require blocked provider routing.

Approval compatibility lacks collision, missing-map, replay, expiry, revocation, scope-key canonicalization, duplicate/unknown action, snapshot-currentness, atomic mutation, and approval-to-execution TOCTOU behavior.

Terminal and file/editor maps omit shell-escape and secret controls, cancel/kill, remote disconnect and partial-write recovery, shared-buffer concurrency, external file changes, unsaved-state preservation, stale worktree validation, and malicious LSP-server boundaries.

Debug auto-ingestion, attach-to-chat, auth handoff, attention_required, takeover, persisted investigation state, and remote scope lack consent, secret/PII redaction, prompt-injection containment, payload bounds, session-hijack prevention, revocation, and deletion behavior.
